about: Jio Platforms Limited, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited, is a technology platform company providing digital connectivity and digital services across India. Through its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), it operates India's largest wireless and fixed broadband network serving 533.3 million customers as of June 30, 2026. The company owns an end-to-end proprietary technology stack spanning network architecture, device engineering, operating systems, and digital applications.

objects.purpose: Prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the Material Subsidiary, RJIL

promoters.background: Reliance Industries Limited is India's largest private sector company by market capitalisation as of June 30, 2026, with diversified operations across energy, retail, media, and digital services.

concentration.note: Serves over 533 million retail and enterprise customers; pre-paid connectivity services contributed 77.08% of consolidated revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026.

litigation_note: The Company, its subsidiaries, promoter, directors and key managerial personnel are involved in various legal proceedings pending before different courts and regulatory authorities.
strengths: Full-stack proprietary technology architecture spanning network core, devices, operating systems, and digital applications.
Market leader carrying ~60% of India's wireless data traffic in Fiscal 2026 with 533.3 million subscribers.
Rapid nationwide 5G standalone rollout with 284.9 million 5G customers as of June 30, 2026.
High subscriber engagement with monthly data consumption reaching 43.7 GB per customer in Q1 Fiscal 2027.
Extensive nationwide reach with 1,059 Jio Centres and 6,322 Jio Points supported by Reliance Retail.
Robust financial performance with Fiscal 2026 EBITDA margin of 51.91% and PAT margin of 20.46%.
Substantial deleveraging with Net Leverage reducing from 0.88x in Fiscal 2024 to 0.36x in Fiscal 2026.

risks.title: Dependence on Material Subsidiary RJIL
risks.detail: RJIL accounted for 87.74% of revenue, 94.88% of EBITDA, and 93.76% of PAT in Fiscal 2026; any operational downturn in RJIL would severely hurt group results.

risks.title: Reliance on Related Party for Prepaid Distribution
risks.detail: Reliance Retail is the sole distributor of prepaid connectivity services, which generated 77.08% of consolidated revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026.

risks.title: Substantial Indebtedness
risks.detail: Consolidated borrowings stood at ₹70,781.00 crore as of March 31, 2026, creating significant debt service commitments and covenant obligations.

risks.title: Licence and Spectrum Renewal Risk
risks.detail: Unified telecom licence of RJIL expires in October 2033; failure to renew licences or acquire spectrum at auctions could disrupt connectivity operations.

risks.title: Regulatory and Net Neutrality Scrutiny
risks.detail: The telecom business is heavily regulated by DoT and TRAI, and subject to net neutrality compliance, tariff directives, and potential licence fee disputes.

risks.title: Dependence on Third-Party Passive Infrastructure
risks.detail: The company relies on a limited set of infrastructure providers for telecommunication towers and optic fibre networks rather than owning them.

risks.title: Intense Market Competition
risks.detail: Intense competition from Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea could constrain pricing power, customer retention, and ARPU expansion.

risks.title: Substantial Ongoing Capital Expenditure
risks.detail: Continuous high capex is required for 5G network densification, fixed broadband penetration, and technology updates, with risk of obsolescence.

notes: Financials for Fiscals 2024, 2025, and 2026 are audited restated consolidated figures; Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY27 stub periods are excluded from multi-year arrays.
